name: I Wanna be the Team Leader
description: Monocarp is a team leader in a massive IT company. There are $$$m$$$ projects his team of programmers has to complete, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$. The $$$i$$$-th project has a difficulty level $$$b_i$$$. There are $$$n$$$ programmers in the team, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. The $$$j$$$-th programmer has a stress tolerance level $$$a_j$$$. Monocarp wants to assign the programmers to the projects in such a way that: each programmer is assigned to no more than one project; each project has at least one programmer assigned to it; let $$$k$$$ programmers be assigned to the $$$i$$$-th project; then all the assigned programmers have to have a stress tolerance level greater than or equal to $$$\frac{b_i}{k}$$$. Help Monocarp to find a valid assignment. If there are multiple answers, print any of them.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$; $$$1 \le m \le 20$$$) — the number of programmers and the number of projects. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the stress tolerance level of each programmer. The third line contains $$$m$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \dots, b_m$$$ ($$$1 \le b_i \le 10^9$$$) — the difficulty level of each project.
output_specification: If there is no valid assignment, print " NO ". Otherwise, in the first line, print " YES ". In the $$$i$$$-th of the next $$$m$$$ lines, print the list of the programmers assigned to the $$$i$$$-th project: first, the number of programmers, then their indices in an arbitrary order. If there are multiple answers, print any of them.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1886E — I Wanna be the Team Leader [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
